newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia on track for needed growth - Access.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia on track for needed growth - Access.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard would get the 4.5 percent economic growth he wants at some stage during the next two years, according to an economic forecaster's report released on Monday.
Access Economics said in its latest quarterly report it expected year-average economic growth of 4.0 percent in the year to June 30, 1998, and 4.6 percent in the year to June 30, 1999.
"There is a significant upturn coming," economist Chris Richardson told Reuters.

"John Howard wants four to four-and-a-half percent growth -- well he won't get that over a long period of time, but he will get it for a solid period of time, basically in financial year 1997/98 and 1998/99," he said.
Howard said last Wednesday that Australia needed economic growth of 4.0 to 4.5 percent a year in order to substantially cut unemployment.
Australian GDP grew at 3.1 percent between the December quarters of 1995 and 1996, while the unemployment rate rose to 8.8 percent in January from 8.6 percent in December.

Access' report said the upturn would stem from waxing world growth and an associated lift in the terms of trade, the three recent interest rate cuts in Australia totalling 1.5 percentage points, solid business investment growth, the housing recovery, and a pick-up in the stock cycle.
"That's an awful lot of things coming at the same time, so the recovery train is starting to leave the station," Richardson said.

The report said the bullish outlook ruled out chances of further rate cuts after the Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy three times between July and December last year, by 50 basis points each time.
It said the recent rate cuts plus the healthy Australian dollar would keep inflation at low levels some time ahead, but this would not last indefinitely.
"We will run out of the good news on inflation coming from the Australian dollar sometime towards the end of 1997 and inflation will bounce back up," Richardson said.
"Instead of being below 2.0 percent, it will start to be around three and as you go into 1998 it'll be back over three again."
Underlying inflation rose 0.4 percent in the December quarter for an annual rate of 2.1 percent.
Access Economics' main forecasts are as follows:
Unemployment (pct) 8.7 8.55 7.6
Employment growth (pct) 1.3 2.4 3.3
Current account (A$bln) -19.88 -21.82 -28.16
